linkedin_post.hook: I nearly let a misleading label ship. A retailer's mother stopped me.
linkedin_post.body:
The Purica label design was approved. Freeze-dried pure Arabica, 100g, ₹559. Lead-free glass jar. Net weight on the front. Bean and process on the back. Clean on screen.

Then a retailer in Mumbai said: "If my mother picks this up, she won't find the chicory line. She'll just taste it and feel cheated."

We had zero chicory to declare. But the template we were using buried the '0% chicory' line on the back panel in 6-point font — the same template brands use to hide 30% chicory.

If the honest brand and the filler brand use the same label layout, the buyer cannot tell the difference.

We rewrote the front panel that night. Bold, Purista, Purica, and Prima now say PURE COFFEE — 0% CHICORY in bold type you can read from across the kitchen counter. Ultra Blend says 70% COFFEE, 30% CHICORY — same size, same prominence, no hiding.

A co-packer in Gujarat offered 18% lower cost if we kept the old template. We walked away.

Today, every SKU passes one test before it ships: if someone reads this jar daily for a year, will they ever feel misled?

Bold: Agglomerated pure coffee. 0% chicory.
Purista: Freeze-dried pure Robusta. 0% chicory.
Purica: Freeze-dried pure Arabica. 0% chicory.
Ultra Blend: 70% coffee, 30% chicory — stated on the front, not hidden in small print.

Revenue lost, trust kept. The label is the only contract that matters.
